newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas still mixed late, fronts up with cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas still mixed late, fronts up with cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained mixed late Tuesday in fairly active trade, with hot weather and firmer physical prices still lifting the front of the complex, industry source said.
At 1420 EDT, July was up by 2.4 cents at $2.27 per million British thermal units, while August was 1.3 cents higher at $2.255. Other deferreds remained narrowly mixed.

"The heat has put a bottom in for the time being. There's no way the market is going to crash right now, but I question how much steam is left (to the upside)," said one East Coast trader, noting prices stalled near resistance again today.

While the heat and some unplanned nuclear plant outages this week, particularly in the East, have helped set a firmer tone for bidweek later in the week, some expected milder weather next week to revive the bears.
"We could see a hiccup (in the rally) later in the week if a cool front comes in (as expected)," a Texas trader said.
In addition, sources said an expected drop in demand in early July due to the Independence Day holiday and some industrial shutdowns also could limit further upside.
In the East, unplanned outages were reported at PECO's 1,055 MW Limerick 1, GPU's 786 MW Three Mile Island 1 and Duke's 846 MW Oconee 3, and all were expected to remain off line for most of the week.

Technical traders said the key to the rally now was a July close above downtrend resistance in the $2.27 area which could set up a test of the $2.36-2.37 area. Further resistance was seen at the contract high of $2.44. Support remained at the $2.151 double bottom, then at $2.13, $2.055 and $2.

In the cash Tuesday, Louisiana Gulf Coast prices firmed slightly to near the $2.30 level. Midcon pipes gained a similar amount to the low-teens. New York city gate gas was quoted about five cents higher in the low-$2.60s.
NYMEX said 36,573 contracts traded at 1350 EDT.
NYMEX July natgas futures expire Thursday, June 26.
On the KCBT, July was still up by one cent at $2.13, while deferreds remained mixed. The East/West spread widened by 1.4 cents to 14.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
KCBT July natgas futures expire Wednesday, June 25.
